from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Standard distance measures physical gaps on a line.",
            "A frog jumps, halving its distance to target.",
            "The sum converges as jumps get smaller."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Usual Notion of Convergence", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#44AAFF")
        number_line = NumberLine(x_range=[0, 4, 1], length=5, include_numbers=True)
        # Using place_in_area as requested per Issue 19
        self.place_in_area(number_line, 'C3', 'C6', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(number_line))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFAA44")
        target = Dot(number_line.n2p(4), color=RED)
        # Using the asset reference as required in Issue 13
        frog = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/frog.svg", color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(frog, 'B3', scale_factor=0.3)
        frog.move_to(number_line.n2p(0))
        
        self.add(target, frog)
        
        curr_pos = 0
        for _ in range(4):
            dist = 4 - curr_pos
            curr_pos += dist / 2
            self.play(frog.animate.move_to(number_line.n2p(curr_pos)), run_time=0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#AAFF44")
        limit_text = Text("Sum -> 4", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        # Using place_at_grid for the limit text as requested per Issue 18/29
        self.place_at_grid(limit_text, 'D4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(limit_text))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Introducing the 2-adic Metric", [
            "2-adic norm measures divisibility by 2.", 
            "Higher powers of 2 mean smaller norms.", 
            "8 is closer to 0 than 2 is."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF44AA"))
        
        # Visualizing 2-adic structure: nested disks using SVGMobject asset
        ruler = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ruler.svg", color="#FF44AA")
        disk1 = Circle(radius=1.5, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.1)
        disk2 = Circle(radius=0.75, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.1)
        disk3 = Circle(radius=0.375, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.1)
        
        group_disks = VGroup(disk1, disk2, disk3, ruler)
        self.place_in_area(group_disks, 'A2', 'C5', scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(group_disks))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#44FF44"))
        
        # Labeling powers
        t1 = MathTex(r"|2|_2 = 1/2", color=WHITE)
        t2 = MathTex(r"|8|_2 = 1/8", color=WHITE)
        
        self.place_at_grid(t1, 'D2', scale_factor=0.7)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Infinite Sums in the 2-adic World", [
            "A series converges if terms shrink 2-adically.",
            "The ultrametric inequality allows unique behavior.",
            "1+2+4+8... converges to -1."
        ])
        
        # Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/abacus.svg
        abacus = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/abacus.svg")
        self.place_at_grid(abacus, "A4", scale_factor=0.3)
        self.play(FadeIn(abacus))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # A series converges if terms shrink 2-adically.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#44AAFF"))
        formula = MathTex(r"|a_n|_2 \to 0").set_color("#44AAFF")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B4", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(formula))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # The ultrametric inequality allows unique behavior.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#44AAFF"))
        ineq = MathTex(r"|a+b|_2 \le \max(|a|_2, |b|_2)").set_color("#44AAFF")
        self.place_at_grid(ineq, "C4", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(FadeIn(ineq))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # 1+2+4+8... converges to -1.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFAA44"))
        sum_eq = MathTex(r"1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + \dots = -1").set_color("#FFAA44")
        self.place_at_grid(sum_eq, "E4", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/calculator.svg
        calc = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/calculator.svg")
        self.place_at_grid(calc, "F4", scale_factor=0.3)
        
        self.play(Flash(sum_eq, color="#FFAA44"))
        self.play(Write(sum_eq), FadeIn(calc))
        
        self.wait(2)

        self.setup_layout("Application: The Geometry of 'Smallness'", lecture_lines)

outline.topic: Exploring the 2-adic Metric: Where Infinite Sums Behave Differently
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate mathematics students or advanced high school students

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Usual Notion of Convergence
sections.content: Recall the standard real-number metric (Euclidean distance). A series converges if the tail terms get 'small' in terms of absolute value (e.g., 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8... = 1). Visualize this as points moving closer on a number line toward a limit.
sections.example: A jumping frog moving toward a lily pad: each jump is half the remaining distance; it never 'overshoots'.

sections.title: Introducing the 2-adic Metric
sections.content: Define the 2-adic norm |x|_2: for any rational number, |x|_2 = 1/2^k where k is the highest power of 2 dividing x. Crucially, higher powers of 2 are considered 'smaller'. This shifts our perspective: 8 is 'closer' to 0 than 2 is.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'P-adic tree': branching factor of 2. Nodes at depth 3 (like 8) are 'deeper' (closer to the root 0) than nodes at depth 1 (like 2).

sections.title: Infinite Sums in the 2-adic World
sections.content: Apply the convergence criterion: a series converges if the terms 'shrink' in the 2-adic metric. This allows for 'bizarre' sums that diverge in standard math. We use the property that |a + b|_2 ≤ max(|a|_2, |b|_2) (The Ultrametric Inequality).
sections.example: The sum 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + ... = -1. Visually, as we add higher powers of 2, the '2-adic distance' to -1 shrinks toward zero.

sections.title: Application: The Geometry of 'Smallness'
sections.content: Summarize how changing the definition of 'distance' transforms the landscape of calculus. In the 2-adic world, every triangle is isosceles, and the space is totally disconnected (like a Cantor set).
sections.example: A data-transmission robot: it experiences 'distance' not by physical meters, but by how many bits of an integer match. Using 2-adic metrics helps optimize error-correcting codes.

improvements.problem: The number line in C3 is too close to the lecture notes, creating visual clutter and potential encroachment.

Labels t1 and t2 are placed too low (E2, E5), creating an awkward gap and poor proximity to the disks.
Formula label t2 is vertically misaligned with the visual center of the disks.
The formula at B2 is too large (scale 1.5), causing it to encroach on the left-side lecture area and create visual clutter.
The inequality at C2 is crowded by the formula above it and poorly balanced horizontally.
The sum equation at E2 is too close to the upper elements and creates a disjointed flow in the vertical grid space.
